newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber trade adrift in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber trade adrift in thin dealings.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market drifted to a quiet close on Wednesday as major buyers checked for price quotes while doing little if any buying, dealers said.
"The big boys are just fishing around to see who will give the lowest offer but they're still holding back and not doing anything," a dealer said.

"They're phoning up, but they believe prices will still head lower so they're not buying at all. I think we'll drift downwards so there's no incentive for a buyer to get into the market," another trader said.
Dealers said the market also took its cue from easier prices in Japan, where the benchmark Tokyo contract shed 1.6 yen to end at 144.0.
"It's a sleepy market. The volumes today were not all that inspiring," a dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 115.75 U.S. cents a kg from 116.75 cents.
May RSS1 was seen at 166.00 Singapore cents (US$1.15) a kg from 167.00 cents. October/December TSR20 was seen at 115.50 U.S. cents a kg from 116.00 cents.
